items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Chick Webb whom I had not met but had heard much talk about... When Chick found out who I was he told me that he had heard about me and some day he was going to have me in his band. I was to hear this statement from Chick many times and would have been very happy if it had ever come true.

ctx.x: Another well known dance hall at 7th Avenue and 138th Street was called the Renaissance. It was not as large as the Savoy but was very nice with a large balcony around three sides of the walls and one big bandstand. Usually private balls were held there and the leader of the regular orchestra or house band was named Vernon Andrade. Most every musician in New York worked for Vernon at one time or another because Vernon did not have a regular bunch of musicians that worked with him. As the Renaissance was not open…

Another place smaller than the Renaissance was the Bamboo which had a band under the leadership of Joe Steel, a fine pianist. And Chick Webb whom I had not met but had heard much talk about, was leading a band at a white dancing school on 125th Street and 7th Avenue which included a trumpeter named Bobby Starke whom I had met at the Rhythm Club.
